# q3dresearch/cookbook

> Reproducible recipes that turn public records into findings. Each recipe is
> one question, one method, one figure, and a written account of what the answer
> cannot support. Python standard library only — no dependencies.

Companion to the wss-* archives at github.com/q3dresearch, which capture public
records their publishers overwrite.

## Start here
- [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md): how to reproduce, verify and extend; inherited failure modes
- [STRUCTURE.md](STRUCTURE.md): repository layout and why
- [VERSIONING.md](VERSIONING.md): method versus data versioning, append-only series

## Recipes
- [dataset-demand-shape](recipes/dataset-demand-shape/README.md): what happens to
  a dataset published on Kaggle. 737,729 datasets; median 8 downloads; 69.5%
  never opened in a notebook; 412,935 with ten downloads or fewer. Size predicts
  use; a sample of already-successful datasets says the opposite.

## Conventions
- provenance.json records corpus hashes and the figures as computed
- history.csv is append-only; method changes are visible breaks, never edits
- if prose and script disagree, the script is authoritative
